title: Invaract Python I/O checker protocol (version 1)
description: Every message the invaract Python package and its checker exchange: one JSON object per line, requests on the checker's standard input and one reply per request on its standard output. A request describes data (names, formats, columns, empty values); it never carries any. A run is `open`, then any number of `read` and `write`/`written` pairs, then `finish`, and, when its reply says to publish, `published` once the outputs are in place. docs/PYTHONIO_PROTOCOL.md describes each message and the order they come in. The version is `open`'s `protocol` and its reply's: it changes only when a message changes in a way an older package or checker would misread; a new optional field is added here without changing it.

Request.description: A request from the package, told apart by `op`.

Reply.description: The checker's reply to one request. `ok` says whether the run may go on; a reply with `ok: false` stops the run from publishing anything.

OpenRequest.description: Starts a run (or, with `check`, a check). The checker reads the settings, resolves the contract, location map and organisational policy, and refuses a contract asking for something it cannot check. Answered by an OpenReply.

protocol.description: The protocol version the package speaks. A checker that speaks another answers not-checked. (The checker takes a request without it as version 1, from packages before the field was sent.)

settings.description: None when absent: the contract then comes from nowhere, and the open is answered not-checked unless `dryRun` is set.

check.description: Only `true` counts (the checker takes any other value as false). true opens a check (`invaract.check`): every declared input counts as read, nothing is published and no events are sent. A check needs a contract.

ReadRequest.description: A read the job made through `invaract.read`, checked as it is made: the name must be a declared input, and its format, columns, CSV options and catalog must agree with the contract. A read without `schema` is one the package has not made because its description already disagrees with the contract: it is refused on that, or, if nothing disagrees, answered not-checked. Answered by an OkReply.

name.description: The input's name in the contract.

location.description: Where the job says it reads (`location=`). Required in a dry run, which has no contract to give it; with a contract, it must be the input's declared location.

format.description: The format the package reads the input in (`parquet`, `csv`, `delta`, `iceberg`, `jdbc`, ...), checked against the input's declared format.

schema.description: The columns read, each with how many empty values it holds.

WriteRequest.description: A table the job hands to `invaract.write`, described before any of it is staged, so a write that cannot pass is refused before the job spends time writing it. Everything but the empty values is checked now: location, format, save mode, catalog, partitioning, CSV options, the inputs read, the columns and their types. Answered by an OkReply; a WrittenRequest for the same name must follow before the run publishes.

name.description: The output's name in the contract.

location.description: Where the job says it writes (`location=`). Required in a dry run; with a contract, it must be the output's declared location.

format.description: The format the package writes, as the job or the contract gives it.

saveMode.description: The save mode the package writes with: `overwrite`, `append`, `error` or `ignore`.

schema.description: The table's columns, with no empty values counted yet.

partitionBy.description: The columns the output is partitioned by, in order; empty for none.

partitionOverwriteMode.description: What an `overwrite` of a partitioned output replaces: every partition (`static`, the default) or only those written.

UnverifiableWriteRequest.description: A write of a table the package could not describe (it offers no Arrow stream). Always refused with UNVERIFIABLE_WRITE; in a dry run, answered not-checked.

unverifiable.description: Why the table cannot be described.

WrittenRequest.description: The end of a staged write whose WriteRequest passed: the verdict on the whole write, with the empty values each column turned out to hold. A required column holding one is refused. The write's event is published now.

nulls.description: How many empty values each column held, by column name.

checks.description: With `runtimeDataQuality` on: what the package found for each of the output's data checks, in the order the OpenReply gave them. A different number of checks than the contract declares is answered not-checked.

FinishRequest.description: The end of the run. Answered by a FinishReply.

completed.description: Always sent by the package (the checker takes a finish without it as completed). false when the job failed: nothing is published, and the checker only delivers its events. A completed run that never wrote a declared output is refused (MISSING_OUTPUT); a dry run's drafts are merged and published.

PublishedRequest.description: Sent once, after a FinishReply whose `publish` is true, when the package has put the outputs in place: each output it published, with what it knows of the data. An output it staged and did not publish (`ignore` on a dataset that holds data, or one put back after a later output failed to publish) is not listed. The checker publishes a WRITE event for each output listed, then the run's JOB_SUMMARY, and delivers the run's events. Answered by an OkReply, or not-checked for an output the run did not stage.

PublishedOutput.description: One output put in place. Every count is what the package knows; one it does not know is left out.

name.description: The output's name in the contract.

rows.description: Every row the run staged for the output: the WRITE event's `rowCount`.

files.description: The files published (plain files), or added by the commit (Delta, Iceberg): `fileCount`.

deltaVersion.description: The Delta table's version after the commit.

icebergSnapshotId.description: The id of the Iceberg snapshot the commit made.

durationMs.description: How long staging and publishing the output took, in milliseconds: `durationMs`.

protocol.description: The protocol version the checker speaks. A package that speaks another stops the run, not checked.

mode.description: `enforce`: a contract is checked, and `contract` gives it. `dry-run`: no contract; every write is let through and a draft contract inferred.

publish.description: Whether the package publishes the staged outputs: the FinishRequest's `completed`. When true, the run waits for a PublishedRequest.

RefusedReply.description: The contract refused the request. The package raises ContractViolation and publishes nothing.

violations.description: The kind of each violation, in order (`OUTPUT_SCHEMA_MISMATCH`, `UNDECLARED_INPUT`, ...): docs-site's Violation Types reference lists them.

explanation.description: Invaract's standard explanation, for a person: what the contract expects, what the job did, why that violates it, and how to correct it.

NotCheckedReply.description: The request could not be checked: a malformed request, a request out of order, a contract that cannot be read, an unknown setting or protocol version. The package raises CheckNotRun and publishes nothing.

Name.description: A dataset's name, as the contract gives it.

Settings.description: Invaract's engine-neutral settings, by their neutral names, as text. The package reads each from the job's environment as INVARACT_<NAME> (`orgPolicy` is INVARACT_ORG_POLICY) and forwards it unchanged. Any other name is answered not-checked.

contract.description: The contract: a file path, or registry://<id>@<version>.

dryRun.description: `true`: no contract; a draft contract is inferred from what the job does.

registryUrl.description: Base URL of the contract registry a registry:// contract is fetched from.

registryClientClass.description: Class name of the registry client (only one built into the checker).

locationMap.description: Path of an id=location .properties file that ref://<id> locations resolve against.

locationUrl.description: Base URL of a location service that ref://<id> locations the location map does not hold are asked of (GET <url>/locations/<id>).

locationTokenEnv.description: Name of the environment variable holding the location service's bearer token: the name, never the token.

orgPolicy.description: Path of an organisational policy document.

orgPolicyOverlays.description: Comma-separated paths of further policy layers.

rejectUndeclaredFields.description: `true`: a column the contract does not declare is refused.

runtimeDataQuality.description: `true`: the OpenReply gives each output's data checks, and each WrittenRequest reports what they found.

jobId.description: The job's stable identity across runs: every event's `job.jobId`.

jobAttributes.description: Facts about this run every event carries (`job.attributes`): comma-separated `key=value` pairs. Malformed pairs are answered not-checked.

contractMetadata.description: Facts about the contract a dry run drafts, put in every draft's `extensions` and every dry-run event's `metadata`: comma-separated `key=value` pairs. Malformed pairs are answered not-checked.

Job.description: Which job the run belongs to, for the events the checker publishes (an event's `job`).

name.description: The job's name: its entry point (`orders_job.main`), or the script's.

libraries.description: The versions of the data libraries the job has loaded (pyarrow, pandas, polars, ...), by name.

Column.description: A column as the package describes it.

type.description: pyarrow's own name for the column's type (`str(field.type)`): `int64`, `large_string`, `timestamp[us, tz=UTC]`, `list<item: struct<sku: string, qty: int32>>`. The checker maps it to the contract's types; a name it cannot map is answered not-checked.

nullable.description: Arrow's nullable flag (true when absent). Whether a required column holds an empty value is judged on `nulls`, not on this flag, where `nulls` is given.

nulls.description: How many empty values the column holds, where the data has been seen (a read; not a write's pre-check).

Catalog.description: The catalog a dataset is registered in, for a catalog table: an Iceberg table (`technology: iceberg`) or a database table (`technology: jdbc`, `catalogName` the database, `namespace` its schema). Checked against the dataset's declared `catalog:` requirement. Files and Delta tables, named by their path, carry none.

CsvOptions.description: The CSV options a CSV read or write used, as text, by the contract's option names (Spark's). Sent only for a CSV dataset that uses some; checked against the dataset's declared `csv:` options.

CheckFound.description: What the package found evaluating one data check over every row it staged.

failed.description: How many rows broke the check.

examples.description: Some of the values that broke it, as text, without repeats; the checker shows at most five.

ContractView.description: What the package needs of the contract: where each dataset is and how it is read or written.

DatasetView.description: A declared dataset: its name and location, its declared columns, and, where the contract gives them, its format, save mode, partitioning and CSV options.

location.description: Resolved: a ref://<id> location has already been resolved through the location map.

partitionBy.description: The partition columns, in order (absent when not partitioned).

OutputView.description: A declared output: a DatasetView, and with `runtimeDataQuality` on, its data checks.

checks.description: The output's data checks, in the order the WrittenRequest reports them.

type.description: The contract's type, as the contract spells it (`long`, `decimal(10,2)`, `array<struct<sku:string>>`).

DataCheck.description: One declared value constraint, as the contract spells it: the field, the constraint type and its properties. A null value never breaks a check.
